olay.intro: Olay is a Procter & Gamble skincare brand sold in mass-market stores worldwide. Its best-known ranges include Regenerist, Total Effects and Luminous, and many of its moisturizers and serums are built around niacinamide, peptides and hyaluronic acid.

paulas-choice.intro: Paula's Choice was founded in Seattle by Paula Begoun, who wrote about cosmetic ingredients before starting her own line. The brand is known for fragrance-free formulas and its exfoliants, above all the Skin Perfecting 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant.

clinique.intro: Clinique is part of The Estée Lauder Companies and launched in 1968 with a dermatologist-developed three-step routine: cleanse, exfoliate and moisturize. The brand describes its products as allergy tested and fragrance free, and Dramatically Different Moisturizing Lotion+ remains one of its signature products.

cerave.intro: CeraVe launched in the United States in 2005 and has been owned by L'Oréal since 2017. The brand says its products were developed with dermatologists, and most of its cleansers and moisturizers contain three ceramides alongside ingredients such as hyaluronic acid and niacinamide.

la-roche-posay.intro: La Roche-Posay is a French brand owned by L'Oréal, named after the spa town whose thermal spring water appears in many of its formulas. Its main ranges include Toleriane for sensitive skin, Effaclar for oily and acne-prone skin, Cicaplast and the Anthelios sunscreens.

neutrogena.intro: Neutrogena is an American skincare brand, now part of Kenvue, the consumer-health company separated from Johnson & Johnson. It is widely sold in drugstores, and its lines include Hydro Boost, the Oil-Free Acne Wash cleansers and Rapid Wrinkle Repair.

drunk-elephant.intro: Drunk Elephant was founded in Houston in 2013 by Tiffany Masterson and has been owned by Shiseido since 2019. The brand leaves out what it calls the Suspicious 6 — essential oils, drying alcohols, silicones, chemical sunscreens, fragrances and dyes, and SLS — and is known for Protini Polypeptide Cream and C-Firma serum.

the-ordinary.intro: The Ordinary is a brand from DECIEM, the Toronto company founded by Brandon Truaxe, in which The Estée Lauder Companies is the majority owner. It sells simple formulas named after their main ingredient and strength, such as Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1%, at low prices.

california-gold-nutrition.intro: California Gold Nutrition is iHerb's own supplement brand. Its range includes collagen, vitamins and joint-support formulas, several of which combine collagen peptides with hyaluronic acid and vitamin C.

dermalogica.intro: Dermalogica was founded in Los Angeles in 1986 by Jane Wurwand and is sold through skin therapists as well as retailers. It is owned by Unilever, and its best-known products include Daily Microfoliant and Special Cleansing Gel.

glow-recipe.intro: Glow Recipe was founded in 2014 by Sarah Lee and Christine Chang, who began by bringing Korean beauty brands to the US before launching their own line. Its products are built around fruit extracts, most famously the Watermelon Glow range.

kiehls.intro: Kiehl's began as a New York City apothecary in 1851 and is now owned by L'Oréal. Its long-running products include Ultra Facial Cream, Midnight Recovery Concentrate and Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado.

tatcha.intro: Tatcha was founded by Vicky Tsai, who based the brand on Japanese beauty rituals, and it is now owned by Unilever. Many of its formulas include a blend of fermented green tea, rice and algae, and The Water Cream is its best-known moisturizer.

the-inkey-list.intro: The INKEY List is a British brand founded in 2018 by Colette Laxton and Mark Curry. Like The Ordinary, it names each product after its key ingredient and keeps prices low, with a range covering hyaluronic acid, retinol, niacinamide and exfoliating acids.

cetaphil.intro: Cetaphil is owned by Galderma and started with a gentle skin cleanser created in 1947. The brand focuses on simple cleansers and moisturizers for sensitive and dry skin, sold widely in pharmacies.

murad.intro: Murad was founded in Los Angeles by dermatologist Dr. Howard Murad and is now owned by Unilever. Its range spans acne, anti-aging and hydration, with products built around retinoids, vitamin C and exfoliating acids.

now-foods.intro: NOW Foods is a family-owned American supplement maker founded in 1968. It makes a wide range of vitamins and supplements, including several hyaluronic acid formulas for joint and skin support.
